Bedside consultation guidance and clinical documentation draft generation for physician review.
Local OCR and structured summarization of laboratory results with pediatric age-specific reference ranges.
Teaching round records and complex case knowledge accumulation into a self-growing knowledge base.
WeChat follow-up assistance generating query lists and reply drafts for physician confirmation.
Daily task management with automated reminders at 17:00 for pending documentation and follow-ups.
Self-growing knowledge base compatible with Obsidian markdown and git version control with daily encrypted backups.

timeline.title: Introduction to Local-First Pediatric AI
talking_points: Introduce the Pediatric Resident AI Assistant as a software solution with a hardware roadmap.
Emphasize 100% local data processing on hospital GPUs.
Clarify that hardware components are in the planning phase.
timeline.spoken: Welcome. Today we present the **Pediatric Resident AI Assistant**, a software solution designed for **local deployment** within hospital infrastructure. [pause] Our system ensures that all patient data remains **on-premise**, processed entirely on local GPU resources. [pause] Please note that while our software capabilities are fully implemented, the accompanying smart badge hardware is currently on the **roadmap** and not yet available for delivery.
timeline.action: Presenter stands beside a slide showing the software architecture diagram and a placeholder image of the smart badge labeled 'Roadmap'.

timeline.title: Challenges in Pediatric Ward Rounds
talking_points: Manual recording and transcription errors during ward rounds.
Loss of chief physician instructions due to unclear speaker identification.
Time-consuming manual entry of laboratory results from HIS screenshots.
Difficulty in tracking follow-up tasks across multiple patients.
timeline.spoken: Pediatric residents face significant administrative burdens. [pause] Manual transcription of ward rounds often leads to **missed instructions**, especially when multiple speakers are involved. [pause] Extracting data from HIS screenshots is **time-consuming** and prone to error. [pause] Furthermore, managing daily follow-ups without a centralized system can result in **overlooked tasks**.
timeline.action: Presenter gestures towards a list of common pain points displayed on the screen, highlighting 'Missed Instructions' and 'Manual Data Entry'.

timeline.title: Software Capabilities Overview
talking_points: Speaker separation for clear attribution of chief physician instructions.
Automated clinical documentation drafts based on bedside consultations.
Local OCR for structured laboratory result summaries.
Integration with WeChat for follow-up management.
Daily task reminders and knowledge base growth.
timeline.spoken: Our software addresses these challenges through **automated transcription** with speaker separation, ensuring chief physician instructions are clearly attributed. [pause] It generates **clinical documentation drafts** for physician review, marking unclear audio as 'to be confirmed'. [pause] Laboratory results from screenshots are converted into **structured summaries** using local OCR. [pause] Additionally, the system assists with **WeChat follow-ups** and provides daily task reminders at 17:00.
timeline.action: Presenter clicks through slides showing screenshots of the software interface for transcription, documentation drafting, and lab result summarization.

timeline.title: Live Demonstration of Implemented Features
talking_points: Demonstrate ward round transcription with speaker labels.
Show generation of an admission record draft from simulated audio.
Display OCR conversion of a sample lab report screenshot.
Highlight the 'to be confirmed' tag for unclear audio segments.
Show the daily task dashboard.
timeline.spoken: Let us demonstrate the **ward round transcription**. [pause] As you see, the system distinguishes between the **chief physician**, resident, and family members. [pause] Here is a generated **admission record draft** based on simulated bedside consultation audio. [pause] Note the **'to be confirmed'** tag where audio was unclear. [pause] Next, we process a **lab report screenshot** locally, extracting values and comparing them against pediatric reference ranges. [pause] Finally, the **daily task dashboard** highlights pending items for review.
timeline.action: Presenter shares screen showing the software interface, playing a pre-recorded simulated ward round audio file and showing the resulting transcription and documentation draft.

timeline.title: Hypothetical Workflow Example
talking_points: Describe a hypothetical day in the life of a resident using the system.
Morning ward round: automatic transcription and instruction extraction.
Afternoon: reviewing lab results via OCR and updating records.
Evening: receiving task reminders and preparing follow-up messages.
Emphasize that this is a simulated scenario, not a real patient case.
timeline.spoken: Consider this **hypothetical workflow**. [pause] During morning rounds, the system captures and transcribes discussions, extracting key instructions. [pause] In the afternoon, the resident uses **OCR** to quickly summarize new lab results. [pause] By 17:00, the system sends a **task reminder**, listing pending documentation and follow-ups. [pause] The resident then uses the **WeChat assistant** to draft replies for parents, which are sent after physician confirmation. [pause] This example illustrates efficiency gains without referencing any real patient data.
timeline.action: Presenter displays a timeline graphic illustrating the hypothetical workflow steps from morning to evening.

timeline.title: Data Sovereignty and Security Design
talking_points: Reiterate 100% local processing on hospital GPUs (RTX 3090).
No data transmission to cloud APIs; raw audio/images deleted after processing.
Knowledge base stored in Obsidian-compatible markdown with git versioning.
Daily encrypted backups.
Compliance obligations must be verified per target market; no certifications claimed.
Include notice: AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.
timeline.spoken: Data sovereignty is central to our design. [pause] All processing, including ASR, OCR, and visual analysis, occurs **locally** on hospital GPUs. [pause] **No data** is transmitted to cloud APIs, and raw recordings or images are **deleted** immediately after processing. [pause] The knowledge base uses **Obsidian-compatible markdown** with git version control and daily encrypted backups. [pause] Please note that specific compliance obligations, such as GDPR or local data laws, must be **verified** according to each target market's requirements. [pause] We do not claim any specific certifications at this stage. [pause] **AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.**
timeline.action: Presenter shows a diagram of the local deployment architecture, highlighting the local GPU and data deletion process, and displays the compliance notice text on screen.

timeline.title: Addressing Common Questions
talking_points: Pricing: Subscription model for software, hardware pricing TBD.
Deployment: Plug-and-play on local hardware, no IT dependency.
Security: Local processing ensures data stays within the hospital.
Certification: No current claims; compliance verification needed per market.
Languages: Supports English, Arabic, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Russian.
Support: Technical support for software installation and usage.
timeline.spoken: Regarding **pricing**, the software operates on a subscription basis, while hardware pricing is **to be determined**. [pause] **Deployment** is designed to be plug-and-play on provided local hardware, minimizing IT dependency. [pause] **Security** is ensured through local processing, keeping data within the hospital firewall. [pause] We make no **certification** claims at this time; compliance must be verified per market. [pause] The system supports multiple **languages** including English, Arabic, and Southeast Asian languages. [pause] **Support** includes technical assistance for installation and usage.
timeline.action: Presenter opens the floor for questions, displaying a slide with the listed FAQ topics.

timeline.title: Next Steps for Interested Hospitals
talking_points: Contact for software demonstration and pilot discussion.
Hardware roadmap availability for future planning.
Emphasis on local deployment benefits.
Reminder that AI outputs are drafts requiring physician review.
timeline.spoken: For hospitals interested in enhancing pediatric care efficiency, we invite you to contact us for a **software demonstration** and pilot discussion. [pause] While the smart badge hardware is on the **roadmap**, our software solutions are ready for **local deployment**. [pause] Experience the benefits of automated clinical documentation and local data sovereignty. [pause] Remember, **AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.** Thank you.
timeline.action: Presenter displays contact information and a QR code for scheduling a demo, ending with a smile and nod.

prompts: How does the system handle multiple speakers during ward rounds?
Can you demonstrate the OCR functionality for lab results?
What happens to the raw audio data after processing?
Is the smart badge available for purchase now?

objections.question: What is the cost of the software subscription and the smart badge?
objections.answer: The software operates on a subscription model with pricing tailored to hospital size and needs. The smart badge is currently on the roadmap, so its pricing is not yet determined. We can provide a detailed quote for the software upon request.

objections.question: Does this require significant changes to our existing IT infrastructure?
objections.answer: No, the system is designed for local deployment on provided hardware (RTX 3090 GPU). It operates independently of your existing IT infrastructure and does not require cloud connectivity, minimizing integration complexity.

objections.question: How do you ensure patient data security and privacy?
objections.answer: All data processing occurs locally on hospital servers. Raw audio and images are deleted immediately after processing, and no data is sent to external cloud APIs. The knowledge base is encrypted and backed up daily. This design ensures data remains within the hospital's control.

objections.question: Do you have FDA or CE certification for this product?
objections.answer: We do not currently hold FDA or CE certifications. Compliance with local regulations such as GDPR or regional data laws must be verified by the hospital according to their specific market requirements. Our focus is on providing a tool for clinical documentation support, not diagnostic decision-making.

objections.question: Does the system support languages other than English?
objections.answer: Yes, the system supports English, Arabic, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, and Russian. This makes it suitable for hospitals in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other regions.

objections.question: What kind of technical support do you offer?
objections.answer: We provide technical support for software installation, configuration, and usage. This includes assistance with setting up the local environment and troubleshooting any issues that may arise during operation.

notices: AI outputs are drafts and require physician review before use.
